definition: Directed attention is the deliberate, effortful focusing of the mind on tasks or information. In this packet, it is described as a limited mental resource that can become fatigued through sustained cognitive demands, especially in urban or high-load environments.

reasons: The packet supports directed attention as a finite resource that can be overused and lead to attentional fatigue, but it does not explicitly support the definition’s wording that it is the “deliberate, effortful focusing of the mind on tasks or information.”

The statement that fatigue occurs “especially in urban or high-load environments” is only partly supported: the packet links urbanization and continuous cognitive demands to attentional fatigue, but it does not establish this as a general defining property of directed attention.
The definition compresses background claims from the article into a broad dictionary-style characterization; several elements are interpretive rather than directly supported by the packet text.

The definition’s phrase that directed attention is “the deliberate, effortful focusing of the mind” is not explicitly stated in the packet text you provided (the packet describes directed attention as a “finite resource” used by persistent cognitive demands, but does not define it in those terms).

The remainder of the definition (directed attention as a finite resource that can lead to attentional fatigue when overused, and that urban/high cognitive-load contexts accelerate attentional fatigue) is broadly supported by the packet, but the unsupported first clause is substantive and prevents passing.
